title: Host the upstream worker with acknowledged startup and drain
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Runledger already owns its loops, leases and retries; a second supervisor policy can interrupt its own shutdown.

## Scope

Register a real generic handler and host the upstream runtime as one critical component. Acknowledge readiness after initialization; stop new claims at drain, allow upstream drain/cleanup to finish, and preserve its returned failures. Document forced-token translation and align outer grace with inner worker budgets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Startup failure, normal drain, worker error, panic/forced-stop limits and partial startup are tested.
- No internal worker loop is respawned under a second policy; direct task and cleanup errors reach the process report.
- Job attempts get fresh execution contexts; request tokens/deadlines are not reused.
- Record attempt counts so layered retries cannot silently multiply durable attempts.
- External effects remain at least once unless the external protocol independently enforces idempotency; document the selected protocol without claiming exactly-once effects.

- examples/postgres-lifecycle/
- crates/batter/src/lifecycle.rs
- docs/integrations.md

title: Exercise cancellation and admission races under sustained scheduling
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Strengthen executable evidence for Batter's small native Rust/Tokio operational contracts: who owns work, what bounds it, who observes failures and when dependencies may close. This makes the foundation easier for AI coding agents to use and modify without guessing hidden framework behavior.

The existing tests cover specific failure paths and two 64-iteration multi-thread races. They do not implement seeded schedule exploration or sustained contention. In the 2026-09-08 audit of commit 5db16f6f18fd918d3d3558a68843120bf9a13b79, all 60 focused admission/lifecycle/operation/process-ownership tests passed a disposable variant that gave descendants independent semaphore capacity. A deterministic capacity-one ancestor/descendant probe passed on the original implementation and rejected that variant. This is a confirmed coverage gap, not a demonstrated production defect. Existing race-loop iteration bounds also do not contain a hung readiness/barrier/result wait.

## Scope

Add test-local seeded scenario generation, controlled scheduling checkpoints and sustained bounded multi-thread stress around completion, readiness, root/descendant admission, drain, forced cancellation and receipt/driver drop. Keep the current deterministic failure-contract tests and add regressions for discovered defects. Implementation fixes must remain scoped to demonstrated contract violations. Do not add a production scheduler, Effect runtime, DI abstraction, resource framework or new public API merely to support the harness.

The scenario families are admission/capacity, operation cancellation/completion, readiness/drain, task/report error retention, driver/receipt ownership and escalation/cleanup. Required cases must be selected explicitly rather than left to chance in a random sample. Keep harness implementation with the foundation tests; generic batter-test-support remains a leaf.

## Contract distinctions for the test oracle

- OperationContext children inherit cancellation downward. Finishing an operation cancels its operation scope; it does not join arbitrary spawned tasks.
- ProcessScope grants descendant admission while its ancestor is active. An already admitted descendant has process lifetime; ancestor completion invalidates further submissions through that scope, not the child's ownership. Roots and descendants share one queued-plus-executing capacity bound.
- Process admission is linearized with drain. Bulkhead cancellation preflight is not atomic with concurrent semaphore acquisition; admitted operations still need their own check/run boundary. Do not invent a stronger Bulkhead guarantee in these tests.
- Owned-driver waiter cancellation and last-owner drop differ from dropping caller-owned run_until. The former preserve the independently driven completion protocol on a live runtime; the latter requests emergency cancellation without promising awaited cleanup.
- Readiness observations and admission decisions must be judged using established happens-before order or contract-permitted overlap, not timestamps sampled after the fact. Likewise, eventual task success is not sufficient to label an abort request false.
- Retain only bounded, generic schedule metadata and numeric test IDs. Do not serialize internal reports or print Debug/Display of application errors/panic payloads. Test diagnostic redaction with synthetic returned-error sentinels and scoped capture; use generic panic-fixture payloads and account explicitly for default panic-hook output without installing library globals.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add a discoverable, bounded multi-thread stress profile for 2 and 4 Tokio workers. For each worker count, exercise at least 32 recorded seeds, 64 supervisor lifecycles, and 4,096 successfully completed finite tasks across those lifecycles. Require overlapping roots/descendants, saturation followed by capacity reuse, and coverage of every scenario family below; fail if a required family or workload minimum was not exercised. Counts are exploration minima, not correctness or throughput claims.
2. Prove shared capacity with a deterministic capacity-one case: while an ancestor occupies the only permit, descendant submission returns Full without invoking its factory. Under mixed contention, independently account for queued plus executing roots and descendants, demonstrate the configured bound, and check rejected factories remain inert. Receipt drop/cancel must neither release capacity early nor cancel admitted work; real completion must permit reuse.
3. Exercise root admission versus drain, active descendant admission during drain, descendant admission versus forced cancellation/task failure, and escaped-scope admission versus ancestor completion. Controlled orderings must check both allowed and forbidden cases; genuinely overlapping calls may take either contract-permitted ordering. A completed drain request forbids later roots; observed force/failure or an expired scope forbids later descendants.
4. Exercise operation completion, explicit cancellation, deadline and future drop with parent/child/sibling contexts. Check downward-only cancellation, parent deadline clamping, scope cancellation on completion/drop, and cancellation-before-deadline-before-completion when branches are simultaneously ready. Preserve the distinct process-descendant lifetime and Bulkhead preflight contracts stated below.
5. Exercise application readiness approval, every component startup acknowledgement, critical exit and drain in competing orders. Ready requires the driver plus approval plus all acknowledgements. Check ordered observations never return to Ready after Draining/Stopped, including acknowledgements/approval attempted after drain has completed.
6. Maintain a bounded test-owned ledger of submissions and expected outcomes, independent of ShutdownReport counters. Reconcile admitted successes, task errors, panics, aborts and unjoined work with receipts and the complete report; preserve all expected task and cleanup error identities/categories without formatting their contents. Mix concurrent failures and dropped receipts. Exercise shutdown-waiter cancellation during cleanup, last-owner drop with retained observers, and caller-owned driver drop before/after first poll under their different contracts.
7. Retain deterministic delayed-coordinator cases proving work finished before escalation keeps its actual outcome and is absent from abort_requested. Exercise completion at drain/cancel boundaries and real unfinished abort targets under stress. A later successful result alone does not prove an earlier abort decision was false. Panic, requested abort or unjoined direct work must keep dependent cleanup conservatively skipped; a joined wrapper proves nothing about detached descendants.
8. Bound each case's waits and each whole profile independently of application shutdown budgets. Configure a maximum 120-second profile allowance and an external watchdog deadline no greater than 150 seconds, plus explicit caps for tasks, event storage and captured output. A deliberately stuck fixture must fail visibly, terminate/reap within the watchdog protocol and retain bounded diagnostics even if Tokio cannot run timers. Watchdog termination is failure containment, never successful application cleanup; record observed timing and scheduler/OS limitations.
9. Provide commands for a fixed seed corpus, a single seed and controlled schedule replay. Record the seed, scenario version, worker count, case/iteration, action/checkpoint order and sanitized outcomes on failure, including watchdog failures. A seed reproduces scenario generation, not the Tokio scheduler. Demonstrate repeatable rejection of an injected fault from a recorded controlled schedule; preserve uncontrolled stress traces as diagnostics and reduce any discovered race defect to a deterministic regression before claiming it is reproducible or fixed.
10. Validate the tests themselves: the shared-capacity test must reject a disposable variant that gives descendants independent permits, and containment must reject the deliberately stuck fixture. Known-bad controls must fail for the intended assertion/watchdog reason, never just compilation or an unrelated timeout. Repeat the unmodified corpus in at least three fresh processes per worker count without retry-to-green behavior. Record exact commands, counts, toolchains, lock hash, platform, results and limitations; run required repository gates for implementation changes. Stress success must remain explicitly non-exhaustive.

title: Separate HTTP observation from request admission and deadlines
description:
## Problem and reproduced evidence

HTTP observation currently shares the request admission/deadline boundary. In crates/batter-axum/src/lib.rs, request_scope_inner constructs the private HttpObservation before the readiness gate. Consequently, gate rejections are already observed, but probes and fallback mounted outside request_scope are not. A downstream consumer removed its outer TraceLayer during adoption and lost those HTTP completion events. The Batter HTTP example also merges probes after applying request_scope, so the coverage problem is reproducible from the recommended composition.

Investigation on 2026-09-08 executed against an actual downstream router using pinned Batter revision e5f2f04b2dbb349d08085caf177f662fcbc89812 and Axum 0.8.9. Its adapter implementation matches the local checkout apart from a platform documentation line. With an INFO tracing capture:

| Scenario | Response status | HTTP completion events |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Application success | 200 | 1 |
| Liveness probe | 200 | 0 |
| Readiness failure | 503 | 0 |
| Unmatched fallback | 404 | 0 |
| Method rejection on an application route | 405 | 1 |
| Drain rejection | 503 | 1 |

On Rust 1.98.1, all 16 Batter adapter tests and all six downstream HTTP tests passed. Their passing results do not establish coverage of this composition: tests/telemetry.rs exercises fallback by installing the combined request_scope across its router. Existing tests/scoped_dispatch.rs proves aborted combined middleware retains the original subscriber and nested span destruction, but does not exercise independent observation.

The disposable reproduction remains at /tmp/batter-http-investigation-zpp1c_u_/src/main.rs on the investigating machine. This is transient supporting evidence, not a required future test fixture; the matrix and assembly instructions here suffice to recreate it using generic routes.

## Delivery scope

Add independent HTTP observation middleware to batter-axum, with no lifecycle handle or deadline policy requirement. Keep HttpObservation private. Add an admission/deadline entry point that retains RequestPolicy, readiness admission, native OperationContext insertion, forced cancellation, and configured failure rendering. Preserve request_scope as a compatibility wrapper over the shared observation and admission implementations. RequestPolicy continues to combine readiness and deadlines; this task separates observation from that combined policy.

Update the HTTP example and adoption guidance to assemble guarded application routes using the admission-only entry point, merge unguarded probes and fallback, apply observation to the assembled router, and apply trusted server request identity outermost. The outer observer must surround middleware that rejects or transforms responses within the intended observed boundary. Migration must replace the inner combined request_scope when adding outer observation, so the supported composition emits one HTTP completion per request. Explicitly document the behavior of nesting the observer with the legacy combined wrapper; do not accidentally promise deduplication.

Preserve first-poll dispatcher capture using batter::telemetry::with_current_dispatch. Observation guards, instrumented futures and their nested spans must all remain inside its protected future through polling and full destruction. Preserve method normalization, matched route templates or <unmatched>, actual response status, outcome and latency, without logging raw paths, query values, headers, bodies, error contents or untrusted methods. Trusted request correlation remains application-owned.

## Axum composition constraint

Axum 0.8.9 Router::layer runs after routing and only covers routes/fallback assembled before the layer is applied. A route appended afterward bypasses it. A literal Tower wrapper outside routing sees no MatchedPath when the current observer creates its span, even for a matched route. Both behaviors were executed in the reproduction. Use the assembled-router placement to preserve sanitized route templates; test new routes added through that normal assembly path and state the late-route limitation. Do not describe the conceptual ordering diagram as literal pre-routing middleware unless route metadata capture is redesigned and tested.

Primary reference: https://docs.rs/crate/axum/0.8.9/source/src/docs/routing/layer.md ; also inspect the resolved axum source and record version-specific semantics in docs/references.md at implementation time.

title: Retain all fixture failures through partial acquisition and teardown
description:
## Outcome and rationale

An early return, panic or cancelled waiter can otherwise lose cleanup or return a lease while pools still use it.

## Scope

Exercise acquisition failure and factory panic separately, then body success/error/assertion panic/cancellation with close/lease/drain failure injection. Do not claim general async Drop or runtime-death cleanup. The outer test fixture runner owns acquisition state, the body task, teardown driving and the retained completion report independently of body/receipt waiters. On a caught body panic, returned error or cancelled body waiter it explicitly drives teardown while the runtime remains alive. Register successfully acquired resources with that owner before exposing them to the body; exercise partial acquisition and factory panic through the same owner. Losing the fixture runner itself or the runtime is outside the completion guarantee.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Retain body, pool-close, lease-cleanup and deferred-drain failures; continue independent cleanup after an error, but never return/reuse a lease when pool quiescence is unproven. - Connections are observably quiescent before lease return. A pool-close failure/timeout test proves unsafe dependent lease cleanup is deferred or skipped and reported, not called clean; subsequent explicit driving is tested when the selected upstream API supports it.
